page: Microsoft Azure D4plds_v6 is an ARM-based virtual machine configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs from an ARM Neoverse-N2 processor running at 3.4 GHz. Operating on Microsoft Hyper-V, the system provides 4 physical cores without simultaneous multithreading, backed by 64 KB L1 data cache, 1 MB L2 cache, and 128 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity is provisioned at 8.0 GB, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory allocation of 2.0 GB per core. The instance includes 236 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and lacks hardware GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results demonstrate balanced throughput across common multi-core processing tasks. The instance achieved a Geekbench multi-core score of 5602.0 and Clang compilation benchmark of 7761.0, alongside average stress-ng ratings. Compression performance is notable, registering 33.06 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip routines. However, cryptographic and mathematical floating-point tests under PassMark ranked lower, reflecting the absence of vector-accelerated instruction sets like AVX-512. Memory bandwidth holds at 90.93 GB/sec for uncached read-only blocks, and static web serving achieves 8.04 GB/sec.

The 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio represents a compute-dense configuration suited for scale-out applications that do not require deep memory footprints. While the bundled 236 GB NVMe SSD provides fast local scratch space, workloads are bounded by the 8.0 GB RAM envelope. The instance delivers competitive resource density for web frontends, build nodes, CI/CD runners, and distributed microservices tailored for the 64-bit ARM architecture.
description: Microsoft Azure D4plds_v6 is a general-purpose, compute-dense virtual machine featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs powered by an ARM Neoverse-N2 processor clocked at 3.4 GHz. The configuration includes 8.0 GB of memory (2.0 GB per vCPU) and a bundled 236 GB local NVMe SSD, operating on Microsoft Hyper-V without GPU acceleration. Synthetic benchmarks highlight consistent performance across general workloads, achieving a Geekbench multi-core score of 5602.0 and 33.06 GB/sec gzip compression throughput. Memory-intensive and cryptographic tests reflect the constraints of its 1:2 memory ratio and instruction set boundaries. The inclusion of local NVMe storage provides high-speed scratch capacity, making the instance an efficient choice for ARM64-native CI/CD build agents, static web serving, containerized microservices, and general scale-out workloads with low RAM requirements.
